# Public Relations Skill for Muse

Turns Muse into an earned-media PR expert for software products. It runs four modes: reactive newsjacking (scored angles within hours of a breaking story — a B+ pitch in the first hour beats an A+ pitch on day three), proactive journalist pitching (beat research, scored media lists, sub-150-word pitches built on a strict quality bar: right beat, real news hook, complete story in the email, specific subject line, clear ask), inbound press requests (HARO, Qwoted, and Featured responses under 200 words), and owned setup (a /press page + media kit checklist: company blurb, founder bios, logo pack, screenshots, coverage list, real contact email — journalists hate forms). It frames stories on three angles — Founding Story, David vs Goliath, Have an Enemy (a broken system, never a competitor) — preps podcast guest appearances as AI-visibility plays (episodes get transcribed and cited by assistants for years), and measures what matters: placements, domain rating, referral traffic, brand-search lift, AI citation rate, and sales conversations citing the coverage — while ignoring vanity metrics like AVE. Its posture is honest about the trade: earned media is a multiplier of distribution, not a substitute — a TechCrunch hit buys legitimacy, backlinks, and AI-citation surface, not 1,000 customers. Discovered via skills.sh. Skills.sh Trust Hub: Pass. Honest note: PR is a momentum game — the skill says to skip it pre-launch with no story beyond "we exist," or if nobody on the team can...
